source_fact: The ingest worker writes records to Postgres synchronously on each request. A queue module exists in queue.py and no request path imports it.
claim_false: The ingest worker has been moved onto the queue.
claim_true: The ingest worker will be moved onto the queue.
decoys: Records reach Postgres during the request that submitted them.
queue.py is imported by no request path.
A slow database write delays the caller.

source_fact: Deploy scripts copy secrets into the container environment at build time. A secrets-manager client is vendored and unreferenced.
claim_false: Secrets have been removed from the build environment.
claim_true: Secrets will have been removed from the build environment.
decoys: A built image carries secret values in its environment.
The vendored secrets-manager client is called from nowhere.
Build-time copying is how secrets arrive.

source_fact: The report endpoint returns every column of the underlying view. No column allow-list is applied and no field is dropped.
claim_false: The report endpoint omits internal columns from its response.
claim_true: The report endpoint will omit internal columns from its response.
decoys: A caller receives internal columns it did not ask for.
No allow-list governs the response shape.
The underlying view determines what is returned.

source_fact: Password reset tokens are generated with the standard library random module and are 6 characters long. Entropy is not configurable.
claim_false: Reset tokens are not guessable within the validity window.
claim_true: Reset tokens will not be guessable within the validity window.
decoys: Token length is fixed at six characters.
The generator is the standard library random module.
Nothing in the configuration changes token entropy.

source_fact: The session middleware reads the legacy cookie before the signed one and returns on the first match. Both code paths are live.
claim_false: The middleware no longer reads the legacy cookie.
claim_true: The middleware will no longer read the legacy cookie.
decoys: A request carrying only the legacy cookie authenticates.
The legacy branch is evaluated before the signed one.
Two cookie formats are accepted.

source_fact: Uploaded archives are extracted to a shared temp directory without path checks. A sanitiser function is defined and unused.
claim_false: Archive members are checked against traversal before extraction.
claim_true: Archive members will be checked against traversal before extraction.
decoys: An archive entry can write outside the extraction directory.
The sanitiser is defined but reached by no caller.
Extraction targets a directory shared across uploads.

source_fact: The audit trail records the actor id and the action name. No before/after values are captured for any field.
claim_false: The audit trail supports reconstructing a changed record.
claim_true: The audit trail will support reconstructing a changed record.
decoys: An audit row names who acted and what they did.
Field values are absent from audit rows.
Reconstruction would require data the trail omits.

source_fact: Rate limits are stored per process in memory. Two replicas therefore permit twice the configured rate.
claim_false: Rate limit state has been centralised in Redis.
claim_true: Rate limit state will be centralised in Redis.
decoys: Scaling out multiplies the effective limit.
Each replica keeps its own counters.
No shared store backs the limiter.

source_fact: TLS 1.3 is compiled into the server binary. The listener config pins the maximum version to TLS 1.2.
claim_false: The server negotiates TLS 1.3 with clients.
decoys: The binary contains TLS 1.3 code.
A client offering TLS 1.3 is answered at 1.2.
The listener config caps the protocol version.

source_fact: The dedupe key is computed from the payload body only. Two identical bodies sent an hour apart collapse to one record.
claim_false: The pipeline distinguishes a genuine repeat submission from a duplicate.
claim_true: The pipeline is designed to distinguish a genuine repeat submission from a duplicate.
decoys: The dedupe key ignores submission time.
Identical bodies produce one record.
Body content alone determines the key.

source_fact: The IAM policy grants s3:GetObject on the whole bucket. A prefix condition is present in a commented-out block.
claim_false: The policy restricts reads to the tenant's own prefix.
claim_true: The policy is configured to restrict reads to the tenant's own prefix.
decoys: The grant covers every object in the bucket.
A prefix condition exists only in a comment.
Any tenant's object is readable under this policy.

source_fact: The retry wrapper is applied to the outbound HTTP client but not to the database client. Database timeouts surface directly to the caller.
claim_false: Transient failures are retried across the service.
claim_true: Transient failures are generally retried across the service.
decoys: Outbound HTTP calls are wrapped in retries.
A database timeout reaches the caller unretried.
The wrapper covers one client and not the other.
